title: GuardFed: A Trustworthy Federated Learning Framework Against Dual-Facet Attacks

C-a.quote: During training, each client update is evaluated for its trustworthiness from two perspectives: its deviation from the reference model and its group fairness performance evaluated on the root data. A dual-perspective trust score is then computed accordingly, and only updates exceeding a predefined threshold are aggregated into the global model.
C-a.locator: Abstract; the two mechanisms are the fairness index and the deviation index, and their SHARED stated purpose is detecting manipulated updates: "To detect whether clients have manipulated their model updates that undermines the performance or fairness of the global model," (Section V-B). The composition is restated at Section V-D, "Specifically, it computes a fairness index that captures the group-level disparity in model predictions, and a deviation index that quantifies the alignment between the client’s update and a reference update trained under fairnessaware reweighting. These two indexes are combined into a unified trust score, and only clients whose trust scores exceed a predefined threshold are selected for aggregation.", and fixed by Algorithm 1, "Compute fairness index Fairn on e D; Compute deviation index Devn by comparing gnt with gst ; Compute trust score: Trustn = Devn · e−τ ·Fairn ; Select trusted clients: S t = {n | Trustn > Γ}". AMENDMENT 3 COUNTS THE FAIRNESS INDEX HERE, AND THE CONTRAST WITH DSFL (2509.08449) IS THE POINT -- see coder_note. C-b.quote: Therefore, additional mechanisms are required to evaluate and filter client contributions based on their utility and fairness, which is the motivation behind the GuardFed framework.
C-b.locator: Section IV; the reason for pairing is complementary threat coverage and the two facets are assigned to the two constituents explicitly at Section V-B, "integrates two components: a fairness index and a deviation index, which respectively assess the update’s potential harm from fairness and utility perspectives.". The threat that motivates the pairing is itself two-faceted, "To address this gap, we introduce the Dual-Facet Attack (DFA), a novel threat model that jointly degrades predictive accuracy and fairness through a combination of model perturbation and sensitive attribute manipulation." (Section I), so the pairing reason is matched to the attack's structure rather than asserted

C-c.quote: We use Accuracy (ACC), Absolute Equalized Odds Difference (AEOD), and Absolute Statistical Parity Difference (ASPD) as evaluation metrics to assess the global model’s learning performance and fairness across different groups.
C-c.locator: Section VI-A; the evidence for the composition is the assembled system's own accuracy and fairness metrics under attack, across COMPAS and ADULT, IID and non-IID, and five attack conditions (Benign, F Flip, FOE, S-DFA, Sp-DFA) against seven baselines plus a hybrid (Tables II and III) -- "In contrast, GuardFed effectively mitigates both poisoning and fairness-harming attacks, including DFA." and "Regardless of the attack variant (S-DFA or Sp-DFA), it achieves high accuracy (above 65% on the COMPAS dataset and 82% on the ADULT dataset) while maintaining low fairness metrics (ASPD and AEOD generally below 0.1).". THERE IS NO ASR OR BACKDOOR METRIC: the attacks are untargeted model perturbation and sensitive-attribute flipping, so C-c is satisfied on the robust-accuracy branch of its frozen text. C-d.quote: We further consider a hybrid defense that directly combines FLTrust and FairGuard, in order to examine whether a simple integration of fairness-preserving and robust aggregation strategies can simultaneously address both performance and fairness threats. Specifically, the hybrid defense first employs FairGuard to select candidate clients for aggregation, followed by FLTrust to assign aggregation weights.
C-d.locator: Section VI-A and Tables II/III; the contrast is on the HYBRID BASELINE THE PAPER CONSTRUCTS, not on the proposed system. The hybrid is sequential (FairGuard selects candidates, then FLTrust weights them), and Tables II and III report FLTrust ALONE, FairGuard ALONE and "Robust FL (hybrid) FLTrust + FairGuard Ours GuardFed" under the same five attack conditions on the same datasets -- so the FLTrust row and the hybrid row hold the downstream mechanism (FLTrust weighting) fixed while the upstream stage (FairGuard candidate selection) is present or absent, which is the direction the rubric requires. The outcome is read off the composed system, "Notably, although the Hybrid algorithm integrates both fairness- and performance-oriented defenses and is expected to achieve robustness on both fronts, it still suffers from increased AEOD and ASPD under DFA.". A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ROUTE is a hyperparameter sweep of the genuinely upstream synthetic-data stage: "(ii) Impact of the server dataset size. To provide a better understanding of the impact of server dataset size, we conduct experiments using varying proportions of server data, ranging from 1% (manually collected root data only) to 10% of the overall dataset size. As shown in the subplots-b of Figure 4, both the testing accuracy and AEOD improve as the server dataset size increases" (Section VI-C), with the trust scoring, the threshold and tau held fixed; the extracted prose does not name the attack condition for subplot-b, and rule 4's benefit of the doubt covers that imperfection. The tau sweep is NOT a route -- it attenuates one factor of the trust score, which changes the combination rule rather than an upstream input

C-e.quote: As τ decreases, the trust score increasingly relies on the deviation index alone, with fairness considerations diminishing; when τ = 0, the trust score depends solely on deviation. Experimental results (Figure 4, subplots-a) confirm that increasing τ from 0.1 to 50 leads to improved fairness (reflected by decreasing AEOD) but results in reduced learning performance.
C-e.locator: Section VI-C; the claim ties a measured change in the composed outcome to the weight given to ONE constituent, with tau = 0 named as the deviation-index-only limit. Constituent-level mechanism claims are also stated for each index separately: "A low (or zero, after ReLU clipping) similarity indicates potential deviation or poisoning behavior." (Section V-C, the deviation index) and "Since our goal is to penalize unfair updates, we apply a negative exponent to the fairness term so that higher unfairness leads to lower trust." (Section V-C, the fairness index)

coder_note:
THE FINDING IN THIS PAPER THAT MATTERS MOST TO OUR ARGUMENT IS NOT ITS CODES: IT BUILDS A TWO-DEFENSE COMPOSITION AND MEASURES THAT THE COMPOSITION FAILS TO INHERIT ITS CONSTITUENTS' GUARANTEES. The hybrid baseline is FairGuard (fairness-attack defense) upstream of FLTrust (Byzantine-robust weighting), constructed for the stated purpose of testing "whether a simple integration of fairness-preserving and robust aggregation strategies can simultaneously address both performance and fairness threats", and the measured answer is no: "although the Hybrid algorithm integrates both fairness- and performance-oriented defenses and is expected to achieve robustness on both fronts, it still suffers from increased AEOD and ASPD under DFA", with the hybrid worse than benign FairFed on fairness (bias around 0.15-0.2). That is EXTERNAL, INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE that composing two defenses does not compose their protections -- the same conclusion Fed-DPRoC (2508.12978) reaches from the opposite direction by proving an invariance result for one particular pair. A3 and A5 should cite both: one paper proves a composition preserves a guarantee, another measures a composition losing one, and neither is our paper. The frame has now produced two live external anchors for the composition question, which is what A4's outcome statement needs.

C-d = YES BY A ROUTE THE FRAME HAS NOT SEEN: THE IDENTIFYING CONTRAST IS ON A BASELINE THE PAPER CONSTRUCTED, NOT ON AN ABLATION OF ITS OWN SYSTEM. C-d's frozen text asks whether "the paper varies the upstream stage while holding the downstream mechanism and the attack fixed"; it does not require the composed system to be the paper's own proposal, and it should not, since what the criterion measures is whether the literature produces the contrast at all. Here FLTrust alone versus FairGuard-then-FLTrust is exactly the RKD "without Clustering" shape -- the downstream weighting rule is unchanged and only what reaches it differs -- run across five attack conditions and two datasets with full outcomes in Tables II and III. This is a SIXTH distinct C-d framing for A5's list (the previous five: named ablation section, upstream-rule substitution, hyperparameter sweep of an upstream knob, analytic characterization, figure-legend-only parameter). It also means a coder searching only for the word ablation would miss it: "ablation" has ZERO hits in this paper.

GUARDFED'S OWN SYSTEM HAS THE HRA SHAPE AND THEREFORE CANNOT SUPPLY THE CONTRAST ITSELF. Trust = Dev * exp(-tau * Fair) composes the two indices as FACTORS in one score, not as stages in a chain, so the tau sweep -- which the paper does run, from 0.1 to 50, and which reaches "the trust score depends solely on deviation" at tau = 0 -- attenuates a factor rather than varying an upstream input to a fixed downstream mechanism. Same reasoning as 2509.18044 (HRA), and the two rows together establish the general point for A5: WHERE A COMPOSITION IS PARALLEL, LEAVE-ONE-OUT AND WEIGHT SWEEPS CANNOT BE C-d IN EITHER DIRECTION, because the upstream/downstream relation the criterion tests is not defined. The only routes left to a parallel composition are a sweep of a stage that is genuinely sequentially upstream of the composite (here the synthetic-data proportion, 1% to 10%, which feeds BOTH indices) or a contrast on some other composed system.

AMENDMENT 3 COUNTS THIS PAPER'S FAIRNESS COMPONENT AND EXCLUDED DSFL'S, AND THE PAIR IS THE BEST EVIDENCE THAT THE AMENDMENT'S PURPOSE TEST DOES REAL WORK RATHER THAN TRACKING THE WORD "FAIRNESS". DSFL (2509.08449) states its reward-penalty ledger's purpose as "a dynamic reward-penalty strategy to enforce fair, adaptive participation over training rounds" -- fairness AS AN OBJECTIVE over clients -- and Amendment 3 excludes it, which cost DSFL its C-a and with it a primary code. GuardFed states its fairness index's purpose as detecting "whether clients have manipulated their model updates that undermines the performance or fairness of the global model" -- fairness AS THE PAYLOAD OF AN ATTACK BEING DETECTED -- and Amendment 3 counts it. The operative words are the purpose for including the component, and the two papers state different purposes for superficially similar machinery. A5 must present this pair, because a reader's first suspicion of Amendment 3 will be that it is applied by keyword.

SCOPE CHECK, RECORDED BECAUSE THE THREAT MODEL IS UNUSUAL FOR THE FRAME: the Dual-Facet Attack combines model perturbation with sensitive-attribute label flipping, so it is a poisoning attack under the frozen screen even though half its objective is fairness degradation rather than accuracy degradation. Inclusion is correct. The datasets (COMPAS, ADULT) and the model are tabular, making this the frame's first tabular-only defense paper alongside HRA's intrusion-detection setting.
